Subject: FintechAI discovery - pricing & latency trade-offs (recap + next steps)

Thanks again for the call today, Alex & Priya — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of needs:
- Use case: customer-facing conversational summaries and contextual recommendations inside the trading desk UI (low-latency critical for UX).
- Peak traffic: ~1.2B tokens/month expected in Q4, with heavy spiky patterns during market open/close windows.
- Important: 95th percentile latency target ~200-300ms for single-turn responses; background batch jobs can tolerate up to 2s.
- Security: SOC2 + VPC required; likely will evaluate Dedicated or Private options.

Cost/price signals you gave on the call:
- Target unit economics: internal target $20-30 per 1M tokens processed (customer goal).
- Budget range: initial procurement target $30k–$75k/month depending on throughput and SLOs.

Trade-offs we discussed (high level):
- Lower latency (200-300ms P95) generally requires smaller batch sizes, higher reserved capacity (Dedicated), and sometimes faster model variants -> increases $/1M tokens.
- Larger batching and KV/prefix caching can lower $/1M tokens significantly but increases tail latency — OK for background processing.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming improves perceived latency for users but may increase per-request overhead.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll send a short pricing options sheet with 3 scenarios (hosted low-latency, dedicated reserved capacity, hybrid burst) for your estimates. (attached)
2) Can you confirm the 1.2B tokens/month is representative of sustained Q4 volume vs a peak-week estimate? Also confirm if the 200–300ms P95 is an absolute hard SLO or a stretch target.
3) If those look right, we’ll loop in Aditya (solutions) and Dev (infra) to sketch batching/streaming config and expected unit economics at each SLO tier.

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Thanks Alex — appreciate the clarity. Attached is the pricing sheet with three scenario buckets and the assumptions baked into each. High-level answers inline below, plus immediate asks for your procurement/engineering review: 

What I attached (redwood_pricing_sheet_v1.pdf):
- Scenario A (Hosted Low-latency): Aim for ~P95 350ms with streaming, aggressive prefix caching — estimated $/1M tokens: $42. Rough estimate for 1.2B tokens = $50.4k/month.
- Scenario B (Dedicated Reserved): Aim for P95 200–300ms with reserved GPUs, smaller batch sizes — estimated $/1M tokens: $28–33 (depending on model variant & quantization). For 1.2B tokens = $33.6k–$39.6k/month.
- Scenario C (Hybrid - Burst + Dedicated): Base reserved capacity for steady state + burst on hosted for peaks — blended $/1M tokens: ~$35. For 1.2B = ~$42k/month.

Key assumptions noted in the sheet (short):
- KV/prefix cache hit rate assumed 40% for scenario A, 60% for B (because of pinning + locality on Dedicated).
- Batching: Hosted low-latency uses smaller max batch (4–8 requests) to meet P95 targets, Dedicated can use larger batching for background flows.
- Streaming: improves perceived latency but adds ~5–10% overhead to total token count due to additional framing and handshake costs.
- Quantization: 4-bit quantization assumed safe baseline for Dedicated pricing; using FP16 variants increases throughput cost but may improve quality for high-risk financial prompts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement: Priya, can we confirm approval process & if we should build a 3-month pilot budget?
2) Engineering: Aditya & Dev — can you validate the P95 200ms Dedicated config feasibility and update expected $/1M tokens given our infra optimizations?
3) If agreed, we’ll schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) next week to align infra and rollout plan.

I’ve included a one-page draft proposal (fintechai_proposal_draft_v1.docx) with scope, trial objectives, and success metrics. Happy to adjust.

—
Marissa

Quick engineering pass — high level feasibility + numbers. This is an internal estimate we can refine in a dedicated deep-dive.

Feasibility:
- Dedicated: Achievable to hit P95 ~200–300ms for single-turn responses with a modest reserved pool. For the model class they described (production LLM ~7–13B equivalent), recommended starting point: 8x A100-class reserved GPUs (or equivalent newer GPU), tuned kernel selection + KV cache co-location. That gives good headroom for 1.2B tokens and peaks.

Streaming overhead:
- Real-world overhead: 5–12% additional token accounting due to framing and early flushes. We use conservative 10% in billing scenarios.

Estimated $/1M tokens (back-of-envelope):
- P95 200ms (Dedicated, small batch, higher reserved cost, 60% cache hit): ~$26–30 per 1M tokens (assumes 4-bit quantization, reserved pricing).
- P95 350ms (Hosted optimize w/ streaming, batch 6–10, 40% cache hit): ~$40–45 per 1M tokens.
- P95 600ms (Batch-first background processing, batch 16–32, 20% perceived latency): ~$18–22 per 1M tokens.

Notes/assumptions:
- Cache hit rates materially affect unit costs; recommend a quick measurement run on sample traffic to validate assumed 40–60% hit rates.
- If FintechAI requires FP16 for certain prompts, all numbers move up ~20–30% on $/1M.
- For peak-week >2B tokens, the hybrid approach (reserve base + hosted burst) reduces peak marginal cost and avoids over-committing GPU capacity.

Deliverables we can provide for Wednesday:
- 3-row table with $/1M tokens and explicit assumptions (batch sizes, cache rate, quantization) — ready to share with the customer.
- Suggested Dedicated reserve configuration and expected latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99) with headroom numbers.

I’ll draft the table and post it in HubSpot + attach to the proposal. If Marissa wants, we can join the deep-dive next Tue/Wed for a quick run-through.
